## Function based data checks {#sec-validate-functional} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ## Motivation We have run through the principles of organised data dictionaries and data validation. Once we understand the consistent types of data(sets) we encounter it is possible to start building data validation **pipelines**. - Pipelines are collections of custom data functions that can apply consistent data cleaning steps to different data that fits a particular layout - Pipelines can help speed up the process of data validation, analysis and plotting. ### Examples - Parameterised reports - simple summary reports that can be generated from a dataset with a button push - Parameterised data import and validation pipelines - our second example and presented here: ## The data In the previous chapters we worked through the process of applying data validation checks to a dataset on female age, fertility and fecundity according to treatments ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} head(female_egg_data) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
| female_id|treatment | age_days| eggs_laid| eggs_hatched| |---------:|:---------|--------:|---------:|------------:| | 1|A | 0| 52.0000| 47| | 2|B | 19| 100.8233| 52| | 3|A | 14| 50.0000| 55| | 4|B | 3| 46.0000| 46| | 5|A | 10| 59.0000| 50| | 6|B | 18| 55.0000| 43|
::: ::: ### Loading and cleaning data In our previous chapters we worked through the steps of importing a dataset, standardising column names, formatting column types and standardising date formats. We also carried out simple exploratory steps using packages such as `skimr`. When we understand the requirements of our data - we can choose to convert code that runs on specific datasets (object-oriented programming) into something more abstract - functional programming. When we have a series of functions - these can be run without modification on new data: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} load_and_clean_data <- function(path, date_col = NULL, delim = ",", show_skim = TRUE) { # Read data using readr df <- readr::read_delim(path, delim = delim, show_col_types = FALSE) |> janitor::clean_names() # Convert date column if provided if (!is.null(date_col) && date_col %in% names(df)) { df <- df |> dplyr::mutate({{ date_col }} := lubridate::dmy(.data[[date_col]])) } else if (!is.null(date_col)) { warning(paste("Column", date_col, "not found in data — skipping date conversion")) } # Optionally skim summary if (show_skim) { cat("\n📊 Quick data summary:\n") print(skimr::skim(df)) } return(df) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} load_and_clean_data("data dictionary/female_egg_data.csv") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 📊 Quick data summary: ── Data Summary ──────────────────────── Values Name df Number of rows 20 Number of columns 5 _______________________ Column type frequency: character 1 numeric 4 ________________________ Group variables None ── Variable type: character ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── skim_variable n_missing complete_rate min max empty n_unique whitespace 1 treatment 0 1 1 1 0 2 0 ── Variable type: numeric ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── skim_variable n_missing complete_rate mean sd p0 p25 p50 p75 p100 hist 1 female_id 0 1 10.5 5.92 1 5.75 10.5 15.2 20 ▇▇▇▇▇ 2 age_days 0 1 17 8.81 0 10.8 19 25 28 ▅▂▂▇▇ 3 eggs_laid 0 1 51.1 12.8 41 45.5 48 52.8 101. ▇▂▁▁▁ 4 eggs_hatched 0 1 44.2 5.18 34 41 44 47 55 ▃▅▇▅▂ ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display}

::: ::: :::{.callout-note} In theory this function could be applied to any dataset (as long as it was in tidy format) ::: ### Validating data ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(assertr) library(dplyr) library(rlang) data_checks <- function(data, metadata_path = NULL, numeric_cols = NULL, character_cols = NULL, unique_cols = NULL, bounded_cols = NULL, bounds = c(1, 30), treatment_levels = c("A", "B"), just_warn = TRUE) { # Define error handler handler <- if (just_warn) assertr::just_warn else assertr::error_stop metadata <- readxl::read_excel(metadata_path, sheet = "Data Dictionary") required_cols <- metadata |> pull(`Name`) # Start pipeline out <- data |> verify(has_all_names(required_cols), error_fun = handler) # Numeric checks if (!is.null(numeric_cols)) { out <- out |> assert(is.numeric, !!!syms(numeric_cols), error_fun = handler) } # Character checks if (!is.null(character_cols)) { out <- out |> assert(is.character, !!!syms(character_cols), error_fun = handler) } # Unique checks if (!is.null(unique_cols)) { out <- out |> assert(is_uniq, !!!syms(unique_cols), error_fun = handler) } # Non-missing checks all_cols <- names(data) if (!is.null(all_cols)) { out <- out |> assert(not_na, !!!syms(all_cols), error_fun = handler) } # Treatment in set if ("treatment" %in% names(data)) { pred_treatment <- assertr::in_set(treatment_levels) out <- out |> assert(pred_treatment, treatment, error_fun = handler) } # Bounded numeric checks if (!is.null(bounded_cols)) { out <- out |> assert(within_bounds(bounds[1], bounds[2]), !!!syms(bounded_cols), error_fun = handler) } # Eggs logic check if present if (all(c("eggs_hatched", "eggs_laid") %in% names(out))) { out <- out |> verify(eggs_hatched <= eggs_laid, error_fun = handler) } return(out) } ``` ::: :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Question :::: ::::{.task-container} Can we think of any ways this code could *potentially* be abstracted/improved further?
